I already have some experience: <experience> Excellent candidates generally achieve low weight (sub-10 range), and balanced, lower axial and bending utilization (axial_uc_max below 0.36, bending_uc_max below 0.7). Specifically, fine-tuning plate thicknesses (`PGRUP_P01` and `PGRUP_PLT` values) and reducing `GRUP_W01` and `GRUP_W02` weights (e.g., `W24X140`/`W24X110` or lower) are key. Modest reductions in the thickness values of `GRUP_DUM`, `GRUP_LG6`, `GRUP_LG6_2`, `GRUP_LG7`, `GRUP_SHF`, `GRUP_STB`, `GRUP_VB1`, `GRUP_VB2`, and `GRUP_VBS` also contribute significantly to weight reduction without drastically increasing utilization.

Poor candidates often have very high or infeasible total utilization (total: -1.0000 or high `max_uc`) or disproportionately high weights from `GRUP_SK2`, `GRUP_SKD`, `GRUP_W01`, and `GRUP_W02` without corresponding reductions in utilization. Avoid large `W24X176`/`W24X150` beams or similar heavy elements if not strictly necessary for bending. Ensure all `GRUP` values are within valid ranges to prevent infeasibility. </experience>You can take advantage of these experience and try to propose better molecules according to the objectives.
